conventions.convention: Assume countable choice. The spatial domain is T³=(R/Z)³ with its Borel product probability measure; characters are exp(2πik·x), and Fourier coefficients use exp(-2πik·x).
w_k=(1+4π²|k|²)^(1/2); H^r has squared norm Σ_k w_k^(2r)|û(k)|². Negative orders are weighted coefficient completions, not necessarily L² functions. Real fields satisfy c(-k)=conjugate(c(k)).
The derivative multipliers are 2πik_j and -4π²|k|². The Leray multiplier is π_kv=v-k(k·v)/|k|² for k≠0, while π_0 is the identity; constants are retained.
P_N truncates to |k|∞≤N. X_N contains real divergence-free coefficients, including the constant mode; N≥1.
Smoothness on the closed time strip means continuous mixed derivatives of every order, with one-sided time derivatives at both endpoints.
The pressure has zero spatial mean and satisfies ∇p=-(I-P)((u·∇)u); the primitive equation is ∂_tu+(u·∇)u=νΔu-∇p.
The common lifespan is T=(2C_sY_0)^(-1) for Y_0>0 and T=1 for Y_0=0; C_s is the commutator constant, not the product constant denoted similarly elsewhere.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the scalar and vector real-order Fourier Sobolev spaces, weights, differential multipliers, divergence-free subspaces, and the commuting orthogonal Leray projection, with u=Pu+∇f and unique zero-mean f∈H^(s+1) for u∈H^s.

Under countable choice, for m≥s>5/2 and divergence-free u∈H^m, the commutator belongs to L² and its norm is at most C_m||u||_H^m||u||_H^s. The two terms are interpreted in H^(-1). For u∈H^(2m), its pairing with Λ^mu equals ⟨(u·∇)u,Λ^(2m)u⟩.

Under countable choice, ||a*b||_ℓ²≤||a||_ℓ¹||b||_ℓ². For σ>3/2, the specified scalar/vector products satisfy ||fg||_H^σ≤2^σW_σ||f||_H^σ||g||_H^σ; vector transport satisfies ||(f·∇)g||_H^σ≤3C_σ||f||_H^σ||g||_H^(σ+1).

For ν≥0, s>5/2 and Galerkin data P_Nu_0 with u_0∈H^s_σ, the higher-order energy inequality holds for every real m≥s. Every approximation exists on [0,T] and ||u_N(t)||_H^s≤2Y_0, with T=(2C_sY_0)^(-1) for Y_0>0 and T=1 otherwise.

Under countable choice, uniformly bounded curves in every H^m, m≥s>5/2, with uniformly bounded H^(m-2) derivatives and the stated Fourier supports admit one subsequence converging in C([0,T],H^(m-1)) for every real m≥s+1. The limit is continuous in every H^m, inherits its bounds, reality, divergence-free condition and convergent initial data.

A continuous curve on [a,b], a<b, in a complete real normed space has a sequence-independent tagged-sum integral, with norm at most (b-a) sup||g||. Its indefinite integral has derivative g, including one-sided endpoint derivatives; integrals are linear, additive over subintervals and commute with bounded linear maps.

Under countable choice, integer s≥4, ν≥0 and smooth divergence-free u_0∈H^s_σ(T³;R³), there exists a smooth projected solution on the stated [0,T], with initial datum u_0, preserved divergence and mean, and ||u(t)||_H^m≤||u_0||_H^m exp(4C_mY_0T) for every real m≥s. Zero data give the zero solution.

concerns.concern: F1 places the vector coefficient block in C^(M_K) and identifies it with R^(2M_K), where M_K counts frequencies. Each coefficient is in C³, so the actual block is C^(3M_K), or R^(6M_K). F2 and proof 1.1 correctly use six real coordinates per coefficient; this is a dimensional typo in F1.

Proof 2.1 says the integrals of S_M e_(-m) equal û(m). This equality holds only once M≥|m|∞; before inclusion of the frequency, the integral is zero. The subsequent limit is valid, but the finite-truncation sentence needs the eventual-inclusion qualification.

The Wiedemann reference describes Theorems 4.14 and 4.16 as existence and higher regularity for periodic Euler and Navier–Stokes. In the opened PDF, Theorem 4.14, printed pp. 31–33, is a viscous strong-solution theorem with a viscosity-dependent lifespan proportional to ||∇u_0||_2^(-4); Theorem 4.16, pp. 34–35, is higher regularity for NSE and uses positive viscosity. They do not supply the Euler case or the viscosity-independent lifespan. The local proof supplies those conclusions independently, so the reference description should distinguish its actual source scope. Source: https://www.uni-ulm.de/fileadmin/website_uni_ulm/mawi.inst.020/skipper/NSEEmilFinished.pdf.

The opening attributes its entire list to the existence and uniqueness theorems, including 'reconstruction of the pressure ... and its uniqueness'. Neither cited theorem states pressure reconstruction, and the remark's deps omit lem-periodic-pressure-reconstruction. That earlier lemma provides exactly the missing support and should be identified for this bullet.

seams_checked.note: The continuum page supplies mathematical spatial-calculus and constitutive context. Its fixed-time Euclidean gradient/divergence and adopted-model distinction agree with the torus conventions. The fluid proofs supply their Fourier calculus locally and do not silently borrow a continuum existence or global theorem.

Opened the fluid postulate and local-evolution consumer. They retain countable choice, smooth divergence-free data, integer s≥4, ν_*≥0, local lifespan, zero-mean pressure and bounded-data continuity. The consumer reconstructs pressure directly from the Leray decomposition and converts dimensionless time to physical time using T_*=L_*/U_*. No empirical or global conclusion is added.

Opened the periodic-shear example. It uses the same unit-torus derivative and projection conventions, distinguishes the steady Euler shear from the decaying viscous solution, and restricts its constant-profile classification to steady unforced periodic viscous shears. Its explicit global Euler example does not strengthen the general local theorem.
